title: apis[].path with an uppercase segment — the grammar still constrains after ADR 0012 widened it
coversRequirement: ADR 0012 — 'Nothing else changes.' Paths remain lowercase; adding '_' to the class widened it by exactly one character
why: ADR 0012 widened the path character class by one character and said nothing else changes: paths remain lowercase, remain rooted at '/', and still admit only segment characters, braces and hyphens. Without a rejecting case the widening is unwitnessed — a pattern accidentally loosened to accept anything would pass adr0012-p1 and no fixture would notice. Case-varying route segments are also a real defect in their own right and not a style question: two paths differing only in case are two routes to the same operation, which means two things to authorize, two things to audit, and a mismatch waiting between whichever one a client calls and whichever one the platform recorded.
notes: MUST BE REJECTED, AND THE REASON MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE OUTCOME. The sole violation in this path is the uppercase 'O' in '/Orders'. The parameter is deliberately left as the legal snake_case {order_id}, because a fixture that rejected on an underscore would be asserting the pre-ADR-0012 grammar and would go green precisely when ADR 0012 had been reverted — a case that rejects for the wrong reason is worse than no case at all. Anyone reading a REJECT here must confirm it is attributed to the uppercase segment and not to the underscore. Report side by side with adr0012-p1: both rejected means the underscore is still banned and ADR 0012 is unimplemented; both accepted means the grammar is not enforced. Decidable by the schema alone; a schema run that accepts this is a real schema defect. Byte-identical to adr0012-p1 apart from the single apis[0].path string, and it declares no Action at scope 'own', so no rejection is attributable to VAL-OWN or AZ7. NOT COVERED HERE: a path containing a space, and a path not rooted at '/'. Both are equally rejectable under the same pattern, but each needs its own single-violation case; they are recorded as gaps rather than folded into this one, because a fixture carrying two violations cannot show which of them caused the rejection.
